sections.text: One motion system, five built-in tools, and room for more: the Rhino changes discipline by changing the tool on its X-carriage, and Klipper changes behaviour to match. Full assembly render: the enclosed machine and its side tower with display and filament bay Feature Rhino Motion CoreXY, 15 mm GT2 belts on X and Y (3 m per belt, 6 m total) Axis travel (from printer.cfg ) X 576 mm, Y 406 mm, Z 295 mm X axis MGW7 linear rail with MGW7H carriage on an aluminium-tube gantry Z axis Three leadscrews (rear T12×2, front T8×2) on kinematic couplings; automatic tramming with Z_TILT_ADJUST Build plate Aluminium heat spreader with silicone heater mats, air-gap insulated; designed as an all-purpose vacuum bed Enclosure 3 mm ACP panels with twin front doors Tool change Tool slides onto the carriage's V-groove, held by one M3×50 bolt and knurled nut; one 21-pin umbilical plug Tools Print heads (BlockOne, SwitchFly), LightSaber laser, HotJoe CNC spindle, DragKnife, plus tools you add Air “Fresh Air” lines: print part cooling, laser blow-air, spindle chip evacuation Controller BTT Octopus (STM32F446) Software Klipper and Moonraker; Rhino Studio, with the Rhino Portal and Tool Manager behind it. Studio slices with Kiri:Moto in the browser or PrusaSlicer on the host; OrcaSlicer and LaserWeb 4 files run too The design files, drawings and build notes are in the Makersmic Rhino-3d-Printer repository on GitHub (see Build reference ). Still in development there: the “Cheeky Monkey” filament box (filament monitoring, air handling, chip exhaust) and a needle-cutter tool.

sections.title: Gantry
sections.text: The X beam is 1″ aluminium square tube (1/16″ wall), lightened with cut-outs made from 3D-printed router templates. The “Bulkup” XY joiners (April 2023) carry extra material at the pulleys and stopped the beam sagging where it meets the joiners. The A/B stepper motors must be no more than 48 mm long with a shaft under 30 mm; they stand on M3×30 mm aluminium standoffs. X gantry beam with the Bulkup XY joiners

sections.title: X-carriage and tool slot
sections.text: The carriage runs on an MGW7 rail and carries the tool lock, the belt clamps and the optical X endstop. A tool slides down into the V-groove on the carriage face, which aligns it, and one M3×50 bolt with a knurled nut (or wing nut) clamps it. X-carriage detail: the tool drops into the wedge-type slot

sections.title: Z axis
sections.text: The bed rides three leadscrews — one T12×2 at the rear, two T8×2 at the front — joined to the plate by kinematic couplings. Each screw is belt-driven through a 2:1 reduction on closed-loop 15 mm GT2 belts of 180–190 mm, and printer.cfg matches it with gear_ratio: 2:1 on all three Z steppers. Because each corner has its own motor, Klipper trams the bed with Z_TILT_ADJUST .

sections.title: Electrical cabinet
sections.text: The BTT Octopus controller switches every heavy load through a DIN-rail relay, which keeps high currents off the board and makes a failed relay a quick swap. Circuit Switched by 12 V low-current: LED and NeoPixel lighting, fans 700-TBR24 6 A relay 12 V high-current: laser module, vacuum pump JQX-13FL 10 A relay 24 V spindle (ESC power) JQX-38F 40 A relay Heated bed mats Solid-state relays Power comes from separate 24 V, 12 V and 5 V supplies. DIN-rail fuse holders protect the stepper motor lines against shorts. Bridgeable distribution blocks spread power; Wago-style blocks (the “Hub”) terminate the umbilical inside the cabinet.

sections.title: The umbilical
sections.text: An essential assembly of the Rhino, the umbilical provides all the connections each toolhead needs. It uses a 21W4 socket connector for every tool connection, with automatic reconfiguration between tool changes, and the umbilical LED strip signals user-specified alarms. Each tool ends in a male 21W4 D-sub (four high-current contacts plus seventeen signal pins); the female half is fixed at the top rear of the frame with the Hub below it. The cable is braided Cat5 plus two 14 AWG conductors. Pins 1, 2, 11 and 12 are the high-current contacts. The pin-by-pin assignment of the umbilical, with the board pin behind each contact, is in Wiring and pin mapping . Each tool's own page in The tools shows which contacts that tool uses. Why every tool has a thermistor. Klipper's extruder expects a temperature reading at all times. Rather than editing printer.cfg for each tool, every tool carries the same thermistor type on pins 3–4 (the laser's is on its heatsink). The swap wizard reads it to confirm the umbilical is seated. Constant connections do not pass through the umbilical; they run to the carriage through the Back Bone : the X endstop (3 wires), the umbilical LED strip, the chamber temperature sensor and two 20 mm air tubes.

Hot-wire cutters, needle cutters, dispensers, pens and other holders, and extra print-head nozzle sizes are added from the Tool Manager (see The Tool Manager portal ). A powered tool takes its main power from an umbilical contact it can share, such as the spindle ESC signal on contact 18, or from a new output on a spare pin, and can switch more outputs on with itself. The next pages are blank tool sheets, two per tool, laid out like the built-in tools' pages. Fill one in for each tool you design. They face each other when the manual lies open: the left page records what the tool is and which umbilical contacts it uses, the right page the settings you enter in the portal (controls, macros, materials) and its parts. Keep the sheet with the tool. Before wiring a new tool, check Pins & outputs in the portal: it shows every contact of the umbilical and what drives it. Only free pins can be given to a new output, and the portal refuses a pin that anything in the config already uses.

The Rhino's software runs on a small computer beside the machine, the host : a Dell OptiPlex 7050, or a Raspberry Pi on older builds. You use it from a browser on any computer, tablet or phone on the same network. YOUR BROWSER THE HOST THE MACHINE Rhino Studio jobs, control, tools, tuning, care, settings Mainsail still there, if you want it Web server serves Rhino Studio rhinostudio.local, :5001 Rhino Portal tools, hardware, care, backups, updates :5000 Moonraker Klipper's messenger: status, commands, files Klipper motion, macros and every safety check Config folder printer.cfg, macros, custom_tools.cfg (from the Portal), variables.save (the mounted tool, tuned values) Controller Octopus board, over USB Motors, heaters and the tool umbilical Rhino Studio talks to Klipper through Moonraker, and to the Portal for everything Klipper doesn't keep Klipper moves the machine and runs the macros: tool swaps, job start and end, and every safety check. It decides what is mounted, and records it in variables.save ; no screen can change that except through Klipper's own swap wizard. Moonraker passes messages between Klipper and the screens: the machine's status, commands, and the job files. Rhino Studio is the main screen. It sends Klipper only commands it has checked, and asks before anything that moves the machine or powers a tool. It slices models in your browser, or on the host with PrusaSlicer if you choose that. The Rhino Portal keeps what Klipper doesn't: the tools you add, system hardware, maintenance, backups, slicing profiles and updates. Studio's Assets, Care and Settings screens use it. It writes custom_tools.cfg from your tools, and asks Klipper to restart only when no job is running. It still has its own pages at port 5000. Mainsail is still installed and works as before; you don't need it.

The Rhino's software comes as one release zip, rhino-config-<version>.zip , which holds the Tool Manager, the Portal and Rhino Studio. The first install goes in once by hand, from a menu on the host. After that, every update goes in from Rhino Studio, with no terminal and no Mainsail.

sections.title: The host
sections.text: The host is a Dell OptiPlex 7050 Micro running Debian 12, with Klipper, Moonraker and Mainsail installed through KIAUH. Its name on the network is rhino . The Raspberry Pi 3B it replaced keeps its SD card as a spare. Setting up a new host, from the BIOS to the first print, is written out step by step in docs/migrate-7050.md ; read its section The move, Nov 3 before you start. Only one host may talk to the controller board. To go back to the spare, shut the 7050 down, move the USB cables to the Pi and start it. Its SD card is unchanged.

sections.title: The first install, from the menu
sections.text: Before you start: nothing printing, and a print head (BlockOne or SwitchFly) mounted . The Z check after the first start homes Z, and only a print head can do that. You need the host's address and its login ( pi ). Copy the zip to the host. In Mainsail open Machine and press Upload , or copy it with scp . Check that the name is exactly rhino-config-<version>.zip ; a browser sometimes adds (1) . Log in to the host from PowerShell, Terminal or PuTTY: ssh pi@rhino.local Open the Rhino menu. Paste one line at a time, with your version in place of 1.9.18: cd ~/printer_data/config unzip -o rhino-config-1.9.18.zip -d ~/rhino-1.9.18 bash ~/rhino-1.9.18/rhino.sh /==========================================================\ | ~~~~ [ Rhino Tool Manager ] ~~~~ | |----------------------------------------------------------| | Installed version : 1.9.17 | | This folder has : 1.9.18 (/home/pi/rhino-1.9.18) | | Portal : running | | Rhino Studio : http://rhino.local:5001 | | by name http://rhinostudio.local | |----------------------------------------------------------| | 1) Preview the install (changes nothing) | | 2) Install / update from this folder | | 3) Install a new zip (unpack, preview, install) | | 4) Undo an install (pick a backup) | | 5) Portal status and recent log | | 6) Restart the portal | | 7) Health check (before and after a move) | | | | Q) Quit | \==========================================================/ Perform action: Preview: option 1. It checks your login, the config folder, whether a job is running and whether port 5000 is free, then lists every step without changing anything. It ends with Dry run finished , or with STOPPED: and what to do. Install: option 2 , then y . It asks for the password once and works through its stages, each ending in OK : backs up the config folder to ~/rhino-backup-<date> ; copies the new files, never touching variables.cfg , variables.save , your positions ( myrhino/positions.cfg ) or the files the Portal writes; keeps the SAVE_CONFIG section at the bottom of printer.cfg , and fixes /home/pi paths if your login is different; starts the Portal at every boot, and serves Rhino Studio at http://rhino.local , http://rhinostudio.local and port 5001. Mainsail moves to port 8090, as a spare until it is removed. Afterwards the menu is always at bash ~/rhino-manager/rhino.sh .

sections.title: First start
sections.text: Open Rhino Studio at http://rhino.local (or http://rhinostudio.local , or the address with :5001 ; some Android phones need the address in numbers). With the print head still mounted: Restart Klipper from the banner, or Settings › Host , and wait for Ready . If Klipper doesn't accept the config, the message names the file and line. Answer which tool is mounted. The question appears on Control , and the top bar shows a confirm button until it is answered (see Rhino Studio at a glance ). Run CHECK_TOOLHEADS in the console on Control . When the line starting rhino: says OK, the tools are loaded. Check Z before the first job. All three Z steppers use gear_ratio: 2:1 . Home with the print head, move Z 10 mm and measure it, then Level the gantry (Bed › Configuration) and check your Z offset. A good place to stop is after the preview (nothing has changed yet) or after the first start. Avoid stopping between the install and the first start.

sections.title: Updating from Rhino Studio
sections.text: Every later release goes in from Settings › Software (see Settings ): Update on the Rhino Tool Manager row downloads the newest release from GitHub onto the Rhino and installs it. Check now looks again. Install from zip takes a zip you downloaded, for a Rhino without internet. Drop it on the panel: it is checked before anything happens, and nothing installs until you press Install . Both are refused while a job runs. The install shows each step with a tick; the Portal restarts part-way, which is expected, and Studio reloads itself on the new version when it's done. Rhino Studio is in the same zip, so it updates with the Tool Manager. Your tools, photos, tuning, maintenance history and settings are kept. Restart Klipper afterwards if the banner asks. Settings › Software: Update, or Install from zip Going back: Go back to … under the drop area installs the zip kept from the version before. If Studio itself won't open, the menu's option 4 lists the backups, previews the restore and asks first; anything added since is moved aside to ~/rhino-undone-<date> , not deleted. Option 7 is a health check that changes nothing, for before and after a move. Never home Z with the laser, spindle or drag knife mounted. Homing Z brings the bed up to the tool. Their macros refuse to, and jobs end with the bed lowered to the safe park height, so X and Y can be homed after a restart without the tool touching anything. Moonraker and the Portal let in only the addresses on the trusted list ( Settings › Trusted addresses ). Keep the Rhino on your home network: the Portal has no login of its own, and anyone on that list can add or remove tools. It can't run G-code, and it refuses to restart Klipper during a job.

Always change tools through the swap wizard. Klipper's safety checks (laser lockout, spindle lockout, job/tool match) all trust the slot the wizard records. Run START_TOOL_SWAP (or press its macro button). A pop-up lists the other tools; pick the one you are installing, then press Start the swap in the confirm window. Nothing moves before that. The machine switches off all tool power, the heaters and the part fan, then waits until the hotend and the bed are below 40 °C. After a hot print this can take several minutes. It parks the head at the swap position ( swap_x / swap_y in myrhino/positions.cfg ), disables the print head's extruder motor and shows Swap the toolhead . Unplug the old tool's umbilical at the top rear of the frame. Undo the knurled nut, remove the M3×50 bolt and lift the tool off the carriage. Slide the new tool down into the carriage's V-groove until it seats, then refit the bolt and nut snug. Plug the new tool's umbilical fully home and route the cable clear of the gantry. Confirm in the pop-up. Every toolhead has a thermistor on contacts 3–4, and the wizard checks it before anything is switched on: if the plug is not fully home it shows Toolhead not detected – reseat the umbilical and press Check again . Only then does a print head's extruder motor get power. While the umbilical is unplugged the nozzle temperature reads about −50 °C; that is expected, and Klipper keeps running. The new slot is saved to variables.save , so it survives a restart. From Rhino Studio: press Swap in the top bar and pick the tool you are fitting. Studio says the machine will cool down and move, and asks first; the wizard's questions then appear as Studio windows, the same as the pop-ups above. After a restart, answer with the confirm button that appears in the top bar. Tool swaps are refused while a job is running or paused. All tool power is switched off before the swap starts. If X and Y are not homed, the swap homes them first with the tool that is on the machine. LightSaber and the Y endstop. Set the Y endstop position for the LightSaber before anything homes Y with it mounted, or the laser reaches the frame first. After any Klipper restart , a pop-up appears about 8 seconds later: Klipper restarted – which toolhead is mounted? Press Yes if the tool shown is the one on the machine, or No – run the swap wizard if it is not. Until you answer, the tool-mounted safety gates stay locked. You can bring the question back any time with RESTORE_TOOL .

Print jobs start from the sliced file. Every other tool starts from a guided setup that walks you through safety checks and setting the work zero, then starts the file for you. This chapter covers what Klipper does once a job starts, for each kind of tool. Preparing the file and pressing Start are in Rhino Studio's Job setup and Preview and Files ; the questions below appear on Control . Pick the material first (non-print tools): SET_TOOLHEAD TOOLHEAD=LightSaber MATERIAL=PLYWOOD . This applies the material's feed, power and acceleration, and the setup wizards read it. It never changes the Z zero.

sections.title: 3D printing (BlockOne, SwitchFly, print-head clones)
sections.text: Slice with the Rhino OrcaSlicer profile for that head (the BlockOne profiles ship in slicer/orca/ ; import them with File › Import › Import Configs ). Its start G-code calls START_JOB with the tool, material, nozzle and extruder, then CALCULATE_PA for pressure advance. Send the file to the Rhino and start it from Files in Rhino Studio (or slice it in Studio's Job setup , which uses the same START_JOB ). START_JOB refuses to run if the file's tool does not match the mounted tool, then homes and shows a confirmation pop-up. With SwitchFly each filament path has its own material: the file names one (or both, as MATERIAL_T0 / MATERIAL_T1 ), and any path left out is asked first – Path 2 (T1) material? , with Same as last time as the first button – while the file waits. The confirmation then lists both paths. It applies the nozzle height saved for that head by the paper test ( NOZZLE_HEIGHT_CALIBRATE , run once per head and kept for it - never by the job), and keeps it when the file is released. With PLA it asks whether to heat the bed or print on a cold bed; a bed that starts below 65 °C warms in stages before Z_TILT_ADJUST . END_PRINT switches off the job's tool and every tool output, clears any work offsets, lowers the bed to the safe park height, moves the head to the park spot (X551 Y381 unless you changed myrhino/positions.cfg ) and runs the staged BED_COOLDOWN . After a job longer than 2 hours it also backs up the config ( BACKUP_CFG ), which can hold Klipper for up to 2 minutes. Controls and system hardware ticked switch off when made safe (an exhaust fan, say) keep running after a normal finish; switch them off when you are done. Cancel, tool swap and the emergency stop still switch them off (1.4.6). Filament change mid-print: FILAMENT_CHANGE pauses, walks you through unload, load and purge, then resumes. FILAMENT_CHANGE , PURGE and PREHEAT only run with a print head mounted (they heat the nozzle), and filament change needs the printer homed. The nozzle heater itself - M104 , M109 or a temperature typed on Control - only switches on with a print head mounted and its thermistor reading normally, and it is switched off within a second if the thermistor ever reads as unplugged while it is on.

sections.title: Setting Z zero (laser, spindle, drag knife, tools you added)
sections.text: Every non-print job sets its Z zero by eye in the same Set Z zero window (the SET_Z_ZERO macro, also a Mainsail button). The job setups open it for you. Bed up / Bed down 10, 1 and 0.1 mm move the bed; up brings the material toward the tool. The window shows the bed height and stops at the travel limits (never lower than Z 290, zero_max_z in myrhino/positions.cfg ). Spindle, knife and added tools: bring the material up until the tool tip just touches its top surface. LightSaber: bring it to the focus point - the smallest, sharpest dot - using Focus dot ON (1%) with laser glasses on. SET – Z zero here makes that bed height G-code Z0 (it is saved, and nothing moves). The job then runs with Z0 there; the laser runs at Z0 with no extra focus offset. After a restart Klipper does not know where the bed is. If the bed was left parked (every job and swap ends with it lowered), the window first asks Bed position – Is the bed still down where it was parked? Yes takes the saved park height as Z and homes X/Y; choose No if the bed was moved by hand with the power off, then home Z with a print head. Choosing a material never changes the Z zero you set. Laser, spindle and knife files must not contain START_JOB : it homes Z, which is refused with those tools mounted. Homing. Z is only homed with a print head mounted and confirmed - the probe is on the print heads. Any other way of homing Z ( Home all on Control, G28 ) is refused with a laser, spindle, knife or added tool mounted, or before the which toolhead is mounted? question is answered after a restart. G28 X Y is allowed with any tool, but Cancel no longer uses it with a laser mounted (see Pause, resume and cancel ). When X/Y are homed while Z isn't, Klipper first lowers the bed 10 mm; if the bed's park height was saved, it is updated to match.

sections.title: Laser (LightSaber)
sections.text: Run LASER_JOB_SETUP FILE=<name>.gcode , then follow the pop-ups: Laser setup – confirm ventilation, glasses, no PVC/vinyl, material flat, extinguisher nearby. Set Z zero – move the bed to the focus point and press SET ; a low-power test mark follows. Check the test mark – Yes to continue, No – set focus again to go back. Ready to cut – set the pass count, then Start the cut . The count is a note for you: the file runs once, so build multiple passes into the file itself. Wear laser glasses from the focus dot onwards: the focus dot and the test mark fire the laser too. Start the cut powers the rail for the file; END_PRINT , cancel, a swap and the emergency stop switch it off.

sections.title: CNC (HotJoe)
sections.text: Run CNC_JOB_SETUP FILE=<name>.gcode : CNC setup – safety confirmations. Set X/Y zero – jog to the corner, then Set X/Y zero here . Set Z zero – bring the material up to the bit tip and press SET . The bed drops clear, the spindle relay switches on and the spindle spins up gently, then to your starting throttle. Ready to cut – nudge the throttle ±5 %, then Start the cut .

sections.title: Drag knife (DragKnife)
sections.text: Run DRAGKNIFE_JOB_SETUP FILE=<name>.gcode : verify the material and blade dial, set Z zero on the surface in the Set Z zero window, cut a test mark, then Cut looks good – continue (or Cut is wrong – help me adjust for blade-dial help) and Start the cut .

sections.title: Tools you added (slot 6+)
sections.text: Run TOOL_JOB_SETUP FILE=<name>.gcode : <tool> setup – the checklist you wrote in the portal; All checked – set work zero . Set Work Zero – Set X/Y zero here , then Set Z zero (the Set Z zero window; the material's Z offset is added on top); Continue . Ready to start – Test pulse fires briefly at low power; then Start – tool power ON (power on for the whole file) or Start – file controls power (the file's own M3 / M5 switch it). Passive tools just show Start . M3 S<value> / M5 in any file control whichever tool is mounted: the laser, the spindle or your powered tool. S is scaled against that tool's S value for full power and never exceeds its power cap.

sections.title: Slicer and CAM settings
sections.text: OrcaSlicer (printing). Make one printer profile per print head (BlockOne, SwitchFly, and any print head you add). In each profile, Printer settings › Machine G-code › Machine start G-code calls START_JOB . Type the tool's name once; OrcaSlicer fills in the rest from the filament and nozzle chosen when you slice: START_JOB TOOLHEAD="SwitchFly" MATERIAL="{filament_type[initial_extruder]}" NOZZLE_SIZE={nozzle_diameter[initial_extruder]} EXTRUDER={initial_extruder} START_JOB parameter OrcaSlicer placeholder Becomes TOOLHEAD typed in each printer profile SwitchFly – must match the mounted tool MATERIAL {filament_type[initial_extruder]} PLA , PETG ... – the filament profile's type NOZZLE_SIZE {nozzle_diameter[initial_extruder]} 0.4 – the printer profile's nozzle EXTRUDER {initial_extruder} 0 or 1 – the first filament used (SwitchFly) Together they pick the tool's material profile, such as PLA_0_4 . Filament type (in the filament profile's settings) must be one of the tool's materials – PLA, PETG, ABS or ASA for BlockOne and SwitchFly; a type such as PLA-CF stops the job at the start with Material PLA-CF_0_4 not defined for toolhead BlockOne . End the file ( Machine end G-code ) with END_PRINT . Pressure advance. On the line after START_JOB , the profile calls CALCULATE_PA with the head's bowden length in centimetres: BOWDEN_LENGTH=5.9 for BlockOne (59 mm), BOWDEN_LENGTH=3.5 for SwitchFly (35 mm, both paths). The other values come from OrcaSlicer placeholders, as in the shipped BlockOne profile: CALCULATE_PA BOWDEN_LENGTH=5.9 MATERIAL=[filament_type] LAYER_HEIGHT=[layer_height] NOZZLE_SIZE=[nozzle_diameter] PRINT_SPEED=[outer_wall_speed] FILAMENT_DIAMETER=[filament_diameter] LINE_WIDTH=[line_width] LaserWeb 4 (laser). Use these machine settings. They replace the older ones in the repository's Laserweb Setup note, which drove pins ( LASERPOWER_pin , VACPUMP_pin ) that no longer exist; going through M3 / M5 keeps the laser lockout, the pause handling and the power scaling. LaserWeb field Value Gcode Start G21 and G90 – homing, focus and work zero are done by LASER_JOB_SETUP Gcode End M5 , then END_PRINT on the next line (switches the laser rail off and parks) Gcode Homing leave blank Tool On leave blank Tool Off M5 Laser Intensity M3 S PWM MIN S VALUE 0 PWM MAX S VALUE 1000 (matches laser_s_max in variables.cfg ) Drag-knife files must not contain M3 : it is refused while the DragKnife is mounted. Use a separate LaserWeb profile with Laser Intensity and Tool Off left blank. CNC files. Spindle speed is set in CNC_JOB_SETUP (the throttle buttons), not by M3 S . An M3 in the file leaves a running spindle alone; M5 at the end stops it.

Pause and cancel work from the job's buttons on Control (or Mainsail's) for every tool. Resume there works only for print jobs; laser, CNC, drag-knife and added-tool jobs resume with the Resume job button in the Rhino pop-up (or TOOL_RESUME ). That Resume refuses whenever the extruder is cold (“not hot enough”), and with a non-print tool mounted it always is. TOOL_RESUME does the same job without that check, and adds the steps a cutting tool needs. Print head Laser CNC spindle Drag knife / passive Powered tool you added On Pause Parks as usual Lift 10 mm, laser off, park Lift 10 mm while spinning, spindle off, park Lift 10 mm, park Lift 10 mm, power off, park Pop-up None <tool> job paused with Resume job / Cancel job same same same Resume with Resume on Control Resume job or TOOL_RESUME same same same On resume As usual Back over the spot, down slowly, laser back to its level Back over the spot, spindle ramps 40 % → its speed (4 s), then down slowly Back over the spot, down slowly Back over the spot, down slowly, power back to its level On Cancel Tool off, bed down, home X/Y, park Laser and rail off, bed down, park without homing X/Y (1.4.5) Spindle off, bed down, home X/Y, park Bed down, home X/Y, park Power off, bed down, home X/Y, park How the resume moves. The head travels to the paused X/Y at its lifted height, drops to 2 mm above the paused height, then makes the last 2 mm at 5 mm/s. Power comes back only once the head is on the paused spot — never at the park corner. If Resume is pressed by mistake on a non-print job, nothing moves: the Rhino pop-up comes back and the console says to use TOOL_RESUME . Refusals. TOOL_RESUME refuses if nothing is paused, or if the recorded tool differs from the one the job paused with. On a print job it simply hands over to the normal Resume. The 10 mm lift is set by variable_lift in _RHINO_PAUSE_HOOK ( tools/tool_power.cfg ); it is reduced automatically when the bed is near the bottom of its travel.

The Portal is the Rhino's record keeper and judge. It runs on the host at port 5000 and keeps what Klipper doesn't: the tools you add, system hardware, maintenance, backups, slice profiles and updates. Every change is checked against your whole Klipper config before it is written. Rhino Studio is where you use it : Assets for tools, hardware, pins and parts, Care for maintenance and Settings for backups and updates (Part 4). The Portal's own pages at http://rhino.local:5000 still work, as a fallback. This chapter covers what the Portal does behind those screens: the steps of adding a tool, which are the same in Studio, the restart rule, and slicing on the Rhino. The pictures are from the Portal's own pages.

sections.title: Adding a tool
sections.text: Press + Add a tool . The wizard's steps depend on the kind of tool: powered tools get all seven, passive tools get a Connector step instead of Outputs and Limits, print-head clones get Hardware. Every kind gets Controls and Macros. Step 1 · Tool – say whether the tool is Additive (adds material: print heads, paste or glue dispensers), Subtractive (removes or cuts material: lasers, spindles, hot wires, knives) or Passive (pens, probes, cameras, holders). Then pick the kind of tool within it, type a name and optional notes. The kind fills in safe starting values; the list of kinds is yours to edit under Admin › Tool lists . The name is what G-code and slicers use: 2–24 letters, digits or _ , starting with a letter. Step 1: category, kind, name and notes Mistakes are caught before you move on, with the rule spelled out: A name that breaks the rules is refused at step 1 Step 2 · Outputs – one row per output the tool needs. Most tools have a main power feed and a signal or two, so press + Add an output for each. Every row has a job and a source: Main power level (PWM) – the output M3 S sets, scaled and capped. Exactly one per tool. Switch on with the tool – an on/off output that turns on when the tool's power does and off with it: a relay, a driver enable line, a vacuum. The source is a contact of the umbilical that a Klipper output already drives (contact 18, the spindle ESC signal, for example), a new output on a spare pin , a piece of system hardware , or another output in the config. Below the outputs, tick the other contacts the tool uses – returns, supplies, the probe – so its pin map is complete. Contacts its outputs drive are ticked for you. Step 2: a PWM signal on contact 18, a relay on contact 11, and the contacts the tool uses Step 3 · Limits – the power cap (a hard ceiling whatever the G-code asks), minimum and idle levels, the watchdog's maximum on-time, and the S value that means full power. Sharing the ESC channel sets the idle level to its neutral 30%. Step 3: power limits and watchdog Step 4 · Materials – the presets you pick when starting a job (power, feed, Z offset), and the pre-job checklist shown before every job with this tool. The material name box suggests the names listed under Admin › Tool lists . Step 4: materials and checklist Step 5 · Controls – extra outputs and inputs the tool brings that are not simply switched with it: a fan with its own speed, a servo, a lid switch. Press + Add a control and answer the guide's questions: you describe what the control does, and the portal works out which Klipper section that needs and shows the exact text it will write. Step 5: the tool's extra controls The control guide asks, in order: Name and purpose. Lower-case letters, digits and _ , such as needle_vacuum . G-code uses the name ( SET_PIN PIN=needle_vacuum ), so it must not match anything else in your config. Which way does the signal go? Rhino controls something on the tool, or the tool sends a signal to Rhino. What should Rhino do with it? Pick the closest match: You pick Klipper section Typical use Switch it on and off output_pin Relay, solenoid, vacuum pump, light, valve Set a level output_pin , pwm: True Driver board, LED dimmer, small heater Run it like a fan fan_generic Fan or blower set by speed, with a kick-start Run it while a heater is hot heater_fan Hotend or heat-break cooling Move it to an angle servo Gate, pen lift, deflector The tool sends a signal gcode_button Lid switch, limit switch, foot pedal, sensor Which pin? Only free tool-connector pins are listed. If myrhino/umbilical.json says what each pin is ( "type": "logic" or "type": "mosfet" ), pins that cannot do the job are greyed out. How does it behave? Active-low wiring and power-up state for a switch; maximum level and PWM cycle time for a level or a fan; heater and turn-on temperature for a heater fan; pulse widths for a servo. Safety and shortcuts. Switch it off whenever the machine is made safe (end of job, cancel, tool swap, EMERGENCY_STOP ; ticked by default); switch it off or leave it on if Klipper shuts down; and make NAME_ON / NAME_OFF (or NAME_SET , NAME_ANGLE ) macros, optionally only while this tool is mounted. The top of the guide: name, direction, what it does and the pin. A new control: name, direction and what it does The bottom of the guide: safety options, the macros it makes, and the exact text written to custom_tools.cfg . Add control saves only a valid entry; a name already in use, a taken pin or two controls on one pin are refused, with the reason in the preview box. Safety options and the text written to custom_tools.cfg For a signal from the tool, the guide asks how it is wired. A switch to ground turns on the pin's pull-up; a sensor that drives the line needs none. Then it asks what happens when the signal triggers and when it is released: show a message, pause the job (only while one is running), emergency stop, or run a command or macro. A lid switch that pauses the job when opened Step 6 · Macros – G-code macros that belong to this tool: a test cut, a purge, a park move. They are written to custom_tools.cfg with the tool and removed with it. Macros your controls made are listed underneath. Step 6: the tool's macros Press + Add a macro . Macro name : letters, digits and _ , saved in capitals because Klipper ignores letter case. Purpose : one line, shown in the macro lists. Only run when this tool is mounted : with another tool on the machine the macro refuses with a message. Macro : Klipper G-code and Jinja exactly as in a [gcode_macro] . The box underneath shows exactly what will be written. Refused: a name used by any macro or Klipper command ( SET_PIN , SWAP_TOOL , PAUSE ), G-code words such as M3 , and template errors such as a missing {% endif %} . Warned: SAVE_CONFIG , FIRMWARE_RESTART or M112 in the body, an unrecognised command (usually a typo), and text after # or ; , which Klipper drops as a comment. A macro with its live preview Step 7 · Review – the portal checks everything against your live Klipper config, warns about shared outputs, and tells you the slot the tool will get. Add up to six photos here, then Create tool . Step 7: review, with the outputs, controls and macros listed Press Add maintenance tasks on the confirmation and the portal offers the Task Book that fits the new tool (see Task Library and Task Books in Part 5). The Task Book offered for a new needle cutter

sections.title: Restarting Klipper to load changes
sections.text: A new or changed tool is saved immediately but is not live until Klipper restarts. A yellow banner lists what is waiting, from the portal or the console; press Restart Klipper when the machine is idle. Changes Klipper never sees – notes, photos, the pin map – are saved without asking for a restart. Changes waiting; the machine is idle, so the restart is allowed While a job is printing or paused, Restart Klipper is greyed out and the banner says why, with the file name, a progress bar, time elapsed and time left, and the clock time when a restart becomes possible. Changes made during a job are saved and queued; only the restart waits, so it can never kill a job. A print running: progress, time left and when a restart is possible Restart automatically when this job finishes is off by default. Tick it and the portal restarts Klipper 30 seconds after the job completes or is cancelled, which leaves time for END_PRINT or CANCEL_PRINT to finish. After an error it does not restart, so you can see what happened. A restart started anywhere else (Studio, Mainsail, RESTART_FOR_TOOLS ) also clears the banner. The console commands ( ADD_TOOLHEAD and the rest) stay refused during a job: they run a shell command that Klipper waits for, which would stall the job's G-code.

sections.title: Slicing for Rhino Studio
sections.text: The portal can run PrusaSlicer on the Rhino for Rhino Studio's Prepare, so a phone or tablet can slice a 3D model without a PC. Prusa ships its Linux build only through Flathub, so the host needs Flatpak once: over SSH, sudo apt install flatpak (the portal never runs sudo itself). Then install PrusaSlicer from Rhino Studio, Settings › Software : it goes in for your login only ( flatpak --user ) and slices a test cube before it is used. The same row offers Update when Flathub has a newer build; if a new build can't slice, the one before is put back, and Go back does the same by hand. It needs a host with 2 GB of memory or more: on a Pi 3B, slice with Kiri:Moto in Studio instead. Each slice runs in Flatpak's sandbox, with no network and no files but its own. Slicing always gives way to the printer: it runs at the lowest priority, one slice at a time, with fewer cores and less memory while a job prints. A host under 4 GB (a 2 GB board, or a Pi 3B with an engine put there by hand) waits until the job is finished. Whatever settings Studio sends, the Rhino's start and end G-code, temperatures, bed and nozzle are always its own. PrusaSlicer is © Prusa Research and the Slic3r authors, under the AGPL-3.0 licence, and is downloaded from Flathub on the machine.

sections.title: Editing and deleting
sections.text: Change a tool you added on its page in Assets ( Edit ), which opens the same steps with its answers filled in. Deleting it frees its pins, removes its photos and archives its maintenance tasks; restart Klipper afterwards. Built-in tools live in variables.cfg and are read-only.

Everything the portal does can also be typed in the Mainsail console. Lines starting rhino: are the tool manager's replies; nothing changes if a command is refused. Managing tools Command What it does ADD_TOOLHEAD NAME=FoamWire KIND=HOT_WIRE PIN=PB1 Add a powered tool on a new pin ADD_TOOLHEAD NAME=Needle KIND=NEEDLE POWER_PIN=SPINDLE_SPEED Add a powered tool on a shared output ADD_TOOLHEAD NAME=Wide KIND=PRINT_HEAD BASE=BlockOne NOZZLES=0.6,1.0 Add a print-head clone with new nozzle sizes EDIT_TOOLHEAD NAME=FoamWire CAP=0.4 MAX_ON_S=300 Change limits (also MIN= , IDLE= , S_MAX= , DEFAULT_POWER= ) EDIT_TOOLHEAD NAME=FoamWire MATERIAL=FOAM_EPS POWER=0.45 FEED=280 ZOFF=0 Add or change a material EDIT_TOOLHEAD NAME=FoamWire DELMATERIAL=FOAM_XPS Remove a material RENAME_TOOLHEAD NAME=FoamWire NEWNAME=HotWire Rename REMOVE_TOOLHEAD NAME=FoamWire Remove (asks you to confirm) LIST_TOOLHEADS Every tool with slot, type and materials TOOLHEAD_PINS Which connector pins are free, used or reserved CHECK_TOOLHEADS Re-check the registry against the config and regenerate custom_tools.cfg RESTART_FOR_TOOLS Restart Klipper to load tool changes (refused during a job) TOOLS_MENU Reminder of where to add, edit and remove tools Running the machine Command What it does START_TOOL_SWAP Guided tool change RESTORE_TOOL Confirm the mounted tool after a restart SET_TOOLHEAD TOOLHEAD=<tool> MATERIAL=<material> Select tool and material for the next job LASER_JOB_SETUP / CNC_JOB_SETUP / DRAGKNIFE_JOB_SETUP / TOOL_JOB_SETUP FILE=<name>.gcode Guided job setup for that tool RHINO_POSITIONS List the positions in myrhino/positions.cfg and check them against the travel limits G28 / G28 X Y Home. Z only with a print head confirmed; G28 X Y with any tool SET_Z_ZERO Set Z zero by eye for the laser (at focus), spindle, drag knife or an added tool – Bed up/down, then SET TOOL_RESUME Resume a paused non-print job M3 S<value> / M5 Mounted tool on / off SET_TOOL_POWER POWER=<0–1> Set an added powered tool's output (fraction of its cap) FILAMENT_CHANGE Guided filament change BED_COOLDOWN Staged, material-aware bed cooldown EMERGENCY_STOP All tool power off (see Safety systems) BACKUP_CFG MSG=<note> Push the config folder to your GitHub backup SWITCH_T0 / SWITCH_T1 MATERIAL=PLA SwitchFly: change filament path. Retracts, moves the servo, heats, loads and purges (the purge lowers the bed to Z5). Without MATERIAL it uses the material chosen for that path at the last job start, and asks if there is none. NOZZLE_HEIGHT_CALIBRATE Paper test for the mounted print head: Down/Up 1, 0.1 or 0.02 mm, then Save. Kept per head; run it once when a head is new or re-seated. Z_TILT_ADJUST Tram the bed with the three Z motors (home first) CALIBRATE_ESC Guided spindle ESC throttle calibration (bit removed) PM_STATUS List maintenance that is overdue or due soon (live) PM_REMINDER Show the start-up maintenance pop-up again

Each of these is automatic; none needs switching on. Tool must match. START_JOB refuses a file sliced for a different tool. The laser and spindle commands refuse to fire unless LightSaber or HotJoe is the recorded tool, and switch their outputs off when they refuse. Shared pin guard. SERVO_LASER is the laser's intensity signal on LightSaber and SwitchFly's filament servo otherwise; servo commands are blocked while LightSaber is mounted. Network changes undo themselves. Changing the hostChanging the Pi's name#39;s name, address, Wi-Fi or power saving (from Rhino Studio, through the Portal) arms a 2-minute undo first; unless you press Keep, it switches back. The only root access is one helper program, /usr/local/sbin/rhino-net , that does nothing else (1.4.8). Feed direction follows the tool. G0/G1 reverse the extruder on SwitchFly path 2 using the saved record of the tool and path. Confirming a swap (or picking another tool after a restart) points that record at the mounted tool, and with SwitchFly turns its selector to path 1 so the servo and the record agree (1.4.7). Power cap. An added powered tool never exceeds its cap, whatever M3 S or SET_TOOL_POWER asks for. Watchdog. Every 5 seconds while an added powered tool is on: with no job running it is cut after the tool's Max time on ; during a pause it is held off; if the tool is no longer mounted everything is switched off. Everything off on the way out. Tool swap, CANCEL_PRINT , END_PRINT and EMERGENCY_STOP switch off the tool on the machine: the laser rail and signal, or the spindle relay (ESC to 0.3 neutral). Swap, cancel, the emergency stop and END_PRINT also switch off every added tool's outputs (1.4.6: END_PRINT for every kind of tool). Controls ticked switch off when made safe are switched off by swap, cancel and the emergency stop; after a normal END_PRINT they keep running, except with an added powered tool, where they go off as before. Nozzle heater guard. The nozzle heater only switches on with a print head mounted and its thermistor reading normally, and is cut within a second if the thermistor reads as unplugged. Z homing guard. Z is only homed with a confirmed print head; with any other tool, or before the restart question is answered, homing Z is refused. Pause makes it safe. See Pause, resume and cancel : lifted clear and powered off before parking. Nothing changes mid-job. Tool swaps, the tool console commands and Klipper restarts are refused while a job is printing or paused. Changes made in the portal are saved and wait for the next restart. EMERGENCY_STOP is a power-off, not a halt. It cuts tool power but does not stop motion. To stop the machine dead, use Stop in Studio's top bar (or M112 ), which shuts Klipper down; then FIRMWARE_RESTART . Start low. Every starting power value (hot wire 40–50 %, caps, maximum on-times) is a placeholder. Test a new tool from a current-limited supply first, then raise its values in the portal while watching it. Hardware layer. Heavy loads (laser, spindle, bed, vacuum pump) are switched through relays, so a controller fault cannot hold them on through the board itself. If Klipper shuts down, the spindle ESC's signal stops and its relay opens. Close the enclosure doors while the laser or spindle runs. Smoke detection is planned in the build notes but not yet fitted. Never leave a laser, hot-wire or spindle job unattended.

Rhino Studio is the Rhino's main screen. It prepares jobs from your models and drawings, previews them, runs the machine, tunes the print heads, and keeps track of the tools, the hardware and the maintenance, all in one web page. It runs in any up-to-date browser on a computer, tablet or phone. The Rhino serves it, so there is nothing to install. Open http://rhinostudio.local , or the Rhino's address followed by :5001 , for example http://192.168.1.50:5001 . Every release of the Tool Manager carries the matching Rhino Studio, so updating one updates both. Rhino Studio, here on Control: the top bar, the rail on the left, and the panels

sections.title: Finding your way
sections.text: The rail on the left holds the screens: Dashboard , Job setup , Control , Bed , Assets , Files , Care and Settings . A number on Care counts maintenance that is due. The top bar shows the mounted toolhead and whether Klipper has confirmed it. Swap lists the other toolheads and starts the swap wizard for the one you pick (see Swapping tools ). After a Klipper restart, a confirm button appears here until you answer which tool is on the machine. Then come maintenance due, the connection, and Stop . Many panels fold away with the arrow beside their title, and Studio remembers that on this device. The ⋯ menu holds the rest of a panel's options. Screens with several pages ( Assets , Bed , Care , Settings ) have a side menu, which folds away with the arrow at its top. Stop sends Klipper's emergency stop ( M112 ) at once, without asking. Klipper then shuts down and needs a restart; use it when something is going wrong, not to end a job. To end a job normally, use Cancel print .

sections.title: What asks first, and the padlock
sections.text: Every command Studio sends is checked first. Anything that moves the machine, switches a tool's power, changes the mounted tool, restarts Klipper or starts a job opens a window saying what will happen, with the exact commands, and waits for Proceed . Heating and plain macros go straight through. The emergency stop never asks. Panels that act on the machine live, such as jogging, live tuning, the bed's lead screws and system hardware, sit behind a red padlock. Press it to unlock. The panel turns red while it's live, and locks again by itself: after 60 seconds without a press, when you leave the page, when a job starts, when the tool changes, or when Klipper stops being ready.

sections.title: Day and night
sections.text: Studio follows your device's light or dark setting. To choose one, or a theme of your own with its own colours, background picture and typefaces, open Settings › Appearance . In every look, red keeps one meaning: stop, or a panel that is live. The same screen in the day look

sections.title: On a phone
sections.text: On a narrow screen the rail moves to the bottom and the panels stack in one column. Pendant mode , from the top of Control, turns a phone into a hand-held pendant: the position, step sizes, square jog keys and Stop . Jogging needs both hands: hold the Hold key with one thumb while you press a jog key with the other. Letting go of Hold stops the next press. The ⇄ button swaps the keys round for left-handed use. Jogging stays locked while a job runs. Control on a phone, and Pendant mode (locked while a job runs)

sections.title: Dashboard
sections.text: The Dashboard is for looking, not for running the machine: it has no machine buttons apart from Stop in the top bar, so it is safe to leave open on a screen in the workshop. The camera fills the page. The tool is at the top left, the machine's state at the top right, and notices at the bottom left; a red notice needs you, and is answered on Control. A row of figures from the Portal's reports runs along the bottom. While a job runs, the job's progress, file, time left and finish time show in large type. For a print, the part being printed appears as a turning hologram over the camera: what's done glows, the layer being printed is an amber line, and the rest is a faint outline. The dial under it shows how much is done, the head's speed and the material. Drag the hologram to turn it; Hide model hides it on that screen. The Dashboard while a print runs Cameras are there to watch, not to keep you safe: a picture can freeze or lag. Studio pauses a camera when it isn't on screen.

Control runs the machine: what the tool is doing, the job, live tuning, jogging, the camera, macros and the console. The panels shown depend on the mounted tool. Flow and Speed appear only with a print head.

sections.title: The status box
sections.text: Across the top: the toolhead (its slot, and whether Klipper has confirmed it), then the readings for that tool, then the job. The status box during a print: the head, hotend, bed, part fan and the job Readings. A print head shows the hotend, the bed and the part fan; a laser shows its power and body temperature; a spindle shows its throttle and body temperature. With no tool mounted, only heaters that are on or still hot show. The small graph beside a temperature shows how it has gone over the last few minutes. Setting a temperature. Click the number, type the new target and press Enter; 0 switches the heater off, and Esc leaves it as it was. The hotend can be heated only with a confirmed print head mounted; switching off is always allowed. The job. How far it has got, the file and a progress bar, with Cancel print (asks first) and Pause or Resume . Resume asks first; Pause doesn't. When no job is running it says Start a job from Files . Tool macros. The row under the box holds the mounted tool's own macros. Show … for other tools lists the rest.

sections.title: Flow and Speed: live tuning
sections.text: Both panels change the machine as it works, so they sit behind the padlock. The values last until Klipper restarts. A print's own settings from the job file, and what the Rhino applies at job start, come back with the next job. Flow: flow, pressure advance, and feeding filament Flow : 50 to 150 %, in 1 % steps or with the slider. Pressure advance : the advance and its smooth time. Feed filament : pick a length (1 to 50 mm) and speed, then Extrude or Retract ; the nozzle must be hot. Not while a job is running. Path picks T0 or T1 on SwitchFly. Speed: speed, Z offset and the speed limits Speed : 10 to 300 % of the job's speeds. Z offset : Closer and Farther move the nozzle in the chosen step, at most 0.05 mm a press, also during the first layer of a print. Reset takes your changes back out. To keep a first-layer height for good, use First-layer squish (see Tuning a print head ). Limits : top velocity and acceleration, until Klipper restarts.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text: Jogging, homing and switching the motors off. The panel is locked to start with; press the padlock to jog. It stays unlocked for 60 seconds after your last press, with the seconds shown on the padlock. Motion, unlocked: one press is one step Pick an X/Y step (0.1, 1, 10 or 50 mm) and a Z step (0.05, 0.1, 1 or 10 mm). One press moves one step. Z+ opens the gap between the tool and the bed. An axis can be jogged only once it is homed, and only with a confirmed tool. Moves stop at the machine's travel limits. Home all , Home XY and Motors off ask first. Jogging locks while a job runs, and when you leave the page, the connection drops, or the tool changes.

sections.title: Camera
sections.text: The picture from the Rhino's cameras; the arrows step through them, and the count shows which one you're looking at. Cameras are added under Settings › Cameras .

sections.title: Macros
sections.text: Each macro is a key. The mounted tool's macros come first; System Macros are the same whatever is mounted, grouped by area, with Other macros folded at the end. A key with a sliders mark takes values: pressing it asks for them, with the allowed range. Macros you make yourself ( Settings › Your macros ) have their own group. System Macros, grouped by area

sections.title: Hardware
sections.text: When the Rhino has system hardware with live controls, such as a case light, an exhaust fan or a chamber heater, the Hardware panel shows each one with its reading and a control to set it, behind the padlock. Tool outputs never appear here: a tool's power is switched by its wizard or a confirmed console command.

sections.title: Console
sections.text: Type a G-code command or macro and press Enter or Send ; ↑ brings back earlier commands. Klipper's replies appear underneath, newest at the top, together with lines from before you connected. The console, newest line at the top A command that moves the machine, switches tool power, changes the mounted tool or restarts Klipper asks first, with what it will do: G28 asks first: it homes the axes

Job setup turns a model or drawing into a job for the Rhino in five steps: File , Process , Setup , Preview and Job file . The steps run along the top of the page. Once the file and the process are chosen, you can go back and forth between Setup, Preview and Job file in any order without losing anything. Going back to File starts over.

sections.title: 1 · File
sections.text: Drop a file on the page, or click to choose one. Job setup takes: 3D models: STL, 3MF and OBJ, for printing or milling; 2D drawings: SVG and DXF, for the laser and the knife; ready-made G-code from another program such as OrcaSlicer or LightBurn. It is checked line by line, the same as a file Studio makes. Drop several models, or several drawings, at once and they become the parts of one job, set side by side. The first file decides the kind; files of the other kind, G-code and files that can't be read are skipped and listed with the reason. Below the drop area, Or start from a toolhead shows each tool with the files, size and materials it takes. Job setup, step 1: drop a file, or start from a toolhead

sections.title: 2 · Process
sections.text: Studio shows the model turning slowly (drag to turn it yourself) and asks What should the Rhino do with it? It lists what each toolhead could do with the file, with the mounted tool marked. Pick one and press Continue . CNC milling takes one part at a time, so it isn't offered for a job with several parts. Step 2: what the Rhino should do with the file

sections.title: 3 · Setup
sections.text: The part sits on the bed in 3D, with the tool, material and settings beside it. Step 3: the part on the bed, and the settings Placing the part. Drag it to move it; drag empty space to turn the view; scroll or pinch to zoom. Angle , Top and Fit part or Whole bed reset the view. Under the bed, Centre X and Centre Y , Turn , Tilt and Scale take exact values; Turn 90° , Turn on X and Turn on Y turn it round the bed's axes; Lay flat then a click on a face puts that face down (Esc cancels). Warnings appear in words: off the bed, too tall, in a keep-out area, over the prime line. The checks in step 5 judge the finished file again. Several parts. Add file , in the header over the bed, or a file dropped on the bed, adds a part. Once there are two, a list of parts appears beside the bed. Click a part, on the bed or in the list, to select it: the fields and the arrow keys then work on that part. Right-click a part (long-press on a phone) for Duplicate , Lay this face flat , Reset way up and Delete from job . Parts that overlap give a warning but aren't stopped. All parts share the settings and are prepared as one file. Toolhead and material. The tool chosen in step 2, and its material and nozzle from the tool's table. The material sets the temperatures, which START_JOB heats to. Settings. A profile (the built-in one, or one you saved with Save as new ; Reset goes back to it), then the settings for the process. For printing, choose the slicer: PrusaSlicer on the Rhino, or Kiri:Moto in this browser. The main settings sit on top; the folded groups below hold the rest. Supports where you choose Supports can be Off , Automatic , or Only where I mark . With Only where I mark, press Mark supports and point at the part: a ring shows where support would go, on the overhang below the pointer. Click to place a mark at the Mark reach size (1 to 15 mm), or press and drag to size it. Click a mark to select it, then change its reach, or remove it with Remove or the Delete key. Erase marks wipes the marks you drag over, and Clear marks removes them all. While supports are on, overhangs steep enough to need them are tinted amber. Marks are kept with that file's job, and stay on the same spot if you move or turn the part. No marks means no support, and the screen says so. Marks are painted on the underside of the part. To see them, look from below: Settings › Appearance › 3D view sets how see-through the bed is from underneath.

sections.title: 4 · Preview
sections.text: Preview prepares the file if anything has changed, then draws every move. Drag to turn it, and scroll or pinch to zoom. Angle , Top and Whole bed reset the view. The layer slider shows the layers up to that point, with the current one strongest. The move slider steps through that layer. Show travel moves adds the moves that don't print or cut. Printed lines are drawn at their real width; supports are drawn in a different shade from the model. Step 4: Preview, the prepared file drawn move by move Preview draws the file, not the macros it calls: a prime line or anything else a macro moves isn't shown. A laser left on during a travel move is drawn as cutting, because the machine really would move with it on. On a slow computer, tick Lighter drawing under the drawing to simplify it; the file isn't changed.

sections.title: 5 · Job file
sections.text: The file's time, filament or cutting length, layers and where it sits on the bed, then the checks it has passed: that it's for this toolhead, has nothing that homes, swaps tools or restarts, ends with END_PRINT , stays inside the bed, under the Z limit and clear of the lead screws, keep-out areas and the prime line. The tool's start and end G-code, if it has any, is named at the top, with a link to change it on the tool's page. Step 5: the checks, Send to Rhino, and Start job once it's sent Press Send to Rhino . The file goes to the Rhino's job files and nothing starts: Sent as … appears. Press Start job beside it. Studio checks the mounted tool matches and Klipper is ready, shows any maintenance that is due, and asks first. If a different tool is mounted, it offers Swap to … instead. Once the job starts, Studio opens Control , where the job's questions and live tuning are. Download saves the file to your computer instead. While a job is running there is no Start button: start the next one from Files when the bed is clear. Nothing queues, on purpose, so a job can't print onto a finished part. Laser, CNC, knife and added tools start through their setup wizard, which walks you through focus, zero and safety checks before the file runs.
Files holds what is stored on the Rhino, in four tabs: Gcode files (the jobs), Config (Klipper's config folder), Logs and Job history .

sections.title: Gcode files: starting a job
sections.text: Each job shows the toolhead it asks for, how it last ran (completed, cancelled or failed, with the date), and a ring if it has never run. A tool button is green when that tool is mounted. Press it to start the job: Studio checks the file against the mounted tool, shows any maintenance due for it, and asks first. If a different tool is mounted, the button offers the swap instead. Gcode files: each job with its toolhead, and how it last ran Upload , or drop files on the page, to add jobs from your computer: several at once, with progress shown. Uploading never starts a job. New file and New folder make an empty G-code file or a folder. Click a folder to open it. Click Name , Modified or Size to sort. Each row's ⋯ menu has Preview , Download , Rename , Duplicate , Move to folder… and Delete . Delete asks first. A file that is printing can't be renamed, moved or deleted. A job's menu To keep the load on the host light, the toolhead is read for the newest 40 files in each folder. Older files in a long folder show without one; tidy them into folders to keep each list short.

sections.title: Preview from Files
sections.text: Preview opens the job on its own page, with the same controls as Job setup's Preview (see Job setup and Preview ), plus Start job (or Swap to … ) and Download . During a job it asks before reading a file, because a big file adds work for the host while the machine runs. Preview of a job on the Rhino

sections.title: Config: editing Klipper's files
sections.text: The Config tab is Klipper's config folder. Click a file to open it in the editor, change it and press Save (or Ctrl+S). Close asks before throwing away changes. Saving keeps a copy of the file as it was in studio_backups , and never restarts Klipper by itself: a bar then offers Restart Klipper to apply (or Moonraker or the cameras, for their files), which can't be pressed while a job is running. Editing printer.cfg Edit only files you know. The files the Portal writes, myrhino/custom_tools.cfg and myrhino/job_hooks.cfg , are rewritten from its own records: change them through Assets instead, or your edit will be lost.

sections.title: Logs and Job history
sections.text: Logs lists Klipper's and Moonraker's logs, read-only; open one to read it or download it to send with a problem report. Job history lists every job Moonraker has kept, newest first, with the total printing time, filament used and longest job at the top. Reprint starts a job again, after the same toolhead check as Gcode files. A file deleted or moved since is marked. Job history

Rhino Studio has four guided tests for a print head, after Ellis' Print Tuning Guide. Each one pushes or prints a little filament, tells you what to look for, and keeps the result on the Rhino, where it is part of the backup. Klipper then applies the results at the start of every job, whichever slicer made the file. Open Assets › Toolheads , select the print head and find its Tuning panel. It shows each test with a tick and the date it was last run, for each of the head's materials and nozzles. Press Tune BlockOne (the button carries the head's name) to open the tests. The Tuning panel on a print head's page: the last run of each test, per material and nozzle The Tune page has two panels. Material picks the material and nozzle for the tests that depend on them, and shows the line a job file must start with to get these results: START_JOB TOOLHEAD=BlockOne MATERIAL=PLA NOZZLE_SIZE=0.4 . Files Rhino Studio prepares always have it. Tests, in order lists the four tests; press Start beside one to run it on this page. The Tune page: the material to test, and the four tests in order Test How often What it sets Kept on the Rhino as Extruder calibration Once per print head, and after any change to its extruder Rotation distance rhino_rd_<head> First-layer squish Per head and material Nozzle height over the paper test rhino_zfine_<head>_<material> Pressure advance Per head, material and nozzle Pressure advance rhino_pa_<head>_<material>_<nozzle> Extrusion multiplier Per head, material and nozzle Flow ( M221 ) rhino_em_<head>_<material>_<nozzle> Run the tests in the order listed: each one assumes the ones before it are right, and a later test reminds you if an earlier one hasn't been run. Every test needs Klipper ready and the head mounted and confirmed. Run pressure advance and the extrusion multiplier again after changing the nozzle, the hotend or the brand of filament.

sections.title: Extruder calibration
sections.text: Checks that when Klipper asks for 100 mm of filament, 100 mm goes in. You need a ruler, a fine marker or a strip of tape, and about five minutes. Press Start beside Extruder calibration . Tick each check under Before you begin once it's true, then press Start . A loose part or a part-blocked nozzle gives a wrong answer here and in every test after it. Extruder calibration: the checks before you begin Press Heat to 210° (the material's printing temperature). The filament is pushed hot, as it is when printing. Mark the filament 120 mm above where it goes into the extruder: hold a ruler along it and put the tape or mark at 120. Once the nozzle is hot, press Push 100 mm . Studio shows the commands and asks first. The filament goes in at 1 mm/s as two 50 mm moves, Klipper's limit for one move, and takes about 100 seconds. Measure from where the filament enters the extruder to your mark, type it in and press Use this reading . Studio works out how much went in and the rotation distance that would have pushed exactly 100 mm. The reading: 21 mm left means 99 mm went in Mark the filament again and push again. The next push uses the new value. When two runs in a row agree within half a millimetre, Studio says ready to save . Press Save … for BlockOne . The panel shows the new value beside the old one. Three runs of 100 mm: ready to save

sections.title: First-layer squish
sections.text: Sets how far the nozzle is from the bed on the first layer, for this head and material. It fine-tunes the head's paper test, so run NOZZLE_HEIGHT_CALIBRATE from Control › Macros first if the head hasn't had one. Studio says so if it's missing. Wash the bed with dish soap and water and dry it with a paper towel, not a cloth. Oil from fingers and fabric softener from towels spoil a first layer more than this test can fix. Tick the checks and press Start . First-layer squish: the checks before you begin Press Make the test . Studio writes a small job, five 30 mm patches of one 0.25 mm layer spread around the bed, into the tuning folder on the Rhino. Press Start job : it heats, homes and sets the nozzle height as for any print. While the patches go down, unlock the padlock (the panel turns red) and press Closer or Farther . Each press moves the nozzle 0.01 mm. Look at each new patch: Too high: round lines with gaps between them; light shows through. Too low: lines fade into each other, the top looks rough or wavy, or ridges build up. Right: lines just touch, the top is smooth and flat, and the underside shows clear lines with no gaps. If you're unsure, a little more squish. When a patch looks right, press Keep this height for PLA while the job is still printing. You can then cancel the rest of the print with Cancel the test print . Squish: Closer and Farther while the patches print What is kept is the difference from the paper test, up to 1 mm either way. At every job start, Klipper adds it to the head's paper-test height for that material.

sections.title: Pressure advance
sections.text: Pressure advance eases the extruder off before a corner and back on after it, so corners stay sharp. Press Make the test , then Start job . The pattern is 21 columns of sharp corners, with pressure advance from 0 to 0.1 in steps of 0.005, left to right. Marks under the columns help you count: a long mark under the 1st, 6th, 11th, 16th and 21st. When it's done, look at each corner under a bright light from the side. Too low: the corner bulges out, and the walls gap on the straight runs. Too high: the corner is dented or thin, with gaps between the walls at the corner. Right: the sharpest corner with the fewest gaps, bulges or dents. If two look alike, take the higher one. Select that column's number. Press Save , or Refine round … to print 11 columns 0.002 apart around your pick, and pick again. Pressure advance: pick the column with the sharpest corner If no column gives a clean corner, or you see gaps and bulges in the same corner, check the extruder itself for loose parts and backlash before tuning further.

sections.title: Extrusion multiplier
sections.text: Sets the flow, so top surfaces fill fully without piling up. Press Make the test , then Start job . It prints six 30 × 30 × 3 mm cubes. From left to right they print at 90, 92, 94, 96, 98 and 100 % flow. When they're cool, compare the tops. Judge the middle of each top, not the edges. Too little: gaps or valleys between the top lines. Too much: a rough top, ridges, plastic piling up at the edges. Right: the lines fill the top as fully as they can without going over. It's noticeably smoother to the touch. Select that cube's number. Press Save , or Refine round … to print finer steps (0.5 %) around it. If all six look alike, press They all look alike for a wider spread, 86 to 106 %. Extrusion multiplier: pick the cube with the smoothest top Hard to tell? Hold a light low beside the cubes so it skims across the tops. On a light colour, scribble a marker across each top and wipe it off: the right one lets the least ink run into the grooves. If you're still unsure, pick the higher one.

sections.title: What the Rhino does with the results
sections.text: Every job starts with START_JOB , which sets up the extruder from scratch for the head, material and nozzle in the job file. Nothing carries over from the job before. Setting When a result is kept When there isn't one Rotation distance The head's result printer.cfg 's value Nozzle height Paper test plus the material's squish The paper test alone Pressure advance The material and nozzle's result An estimate from CALCULATE_PA Flow The material and nozzle's result 100 % The console shows one line per job saying which values it used and where each came from: tuned , or printer.cfg . CALCULATE_PA runs just after START_JOB in every slicer profile. When the material has a tuned pressure advance it keeps that one and says (tuned) ; otherwise it estimates one from the Bowden length and the material. The material name must match. A file from another slicer must call the material by the Rhino's name, such as PLA and not PLA+ . If the slicer's name differs from the job's, a red console line says so and the job's material is used. If no head is mapped to the tool, CALCULATE_PA says so in red and leaves pressure advance as it is. A kept value outside its sane range (rotation distance 0.1–100, pressure advance 0–1, flow 50–150 %) is ignored and reported, and printer.cfg 's value is used. Tune it again if you see that message. Results saved before Tool Manager 1.9.17 were kept only in Studio. The Not on the Rhino yet panel on the Tune page lists them; press Store on the Rhino so Klipper uses them too.

Bed on Rhino Studio's left rail has two pages, chosen from its side menu. Bed mesh shows how flat the bed is and the meshes Klipper follows. Configuration moves single Z lead screws when the bed is too far off level for Z-tilt to fix.

sections.title: Bed mesh
sections.text: The page shows the bed from above, as you stand at the front. The top line says which mesh Klipper is using, with its bed temperature, the head that probed it and when; Switch off stops moves from following it. Looking at a mesh here changes nothing on the machine. Only Use does. Bed mesh: the mesh in use, seen from above Map : Shape shows the heights as probed; blue is lower, amber higher, and the numbers are in millimetres. Without tilt takes out the slope that levelling the gantry would remove, leaving the warp of the plate itself. Compare shows this mesh minus another one you choose, such as the same bed probed cold and hot. Untick Numbers for a plain map. Reading : Range , between the highest and lowest point, and how much of a first layer that is; Tilt , the slope to the right and to the back; and Warp , what is left with the tilt taken out. Meshes : the meshes Klipper holds, with Use and Remove . New and removed meshes last only until Klipper restarts; Save to printer.cfg keeps them, and restarts Klipper. Make a mesh : the bed temperature, the time at temperature before probing, and whether to level the gantry first ( Z_TILT_ADJUST ). While a job runs, the page only shows meshes: a print loads its own mesh at the start.

sections.title: Configuration: moving one lead screw
sections.text: The Rhino's bed rides on three Z lead screws, each with its own motor. Z_TILT_ADJUST ( Level the gantry ) probes the bed and turns each screw until the bed is level. If the bed is too far off to start with, Z-tilt stops with Move out of range . This page lets you bring the bed close by eye first, by moving the screws you choose. Nothing on this page is saved. Bed › Configuration: the lead screws, the controls to move them, and Home and level The Lead screws panel shows the bed from above with each lead screw just off its corner or edge: front left, rear centre and front right on the Rhino. The screws are drawn by place, not to scale. The crosses are where Z-tilt probes. Each screw's card shows its name, its motor ( stepper_z , stepper_z1 …), how far it has moved since you unlocked, and what the last Z-tilt asked of it. Tick a screw's box to choose it. Tick the screw or screws to move. In Move screws , press the padlock. Studio asks once and shows what will run. Unlocking asks once, and says Z will be marked not homed Press Unlock for 60 s . The panel turns red. Choose a step: 0.1, 0.5, 1 or 5 mm. Up raises the bed at the ticked screws and Down lowers it, one motor after another. Each card shows how far its screw has moved (+ is up). Repeat until the bed looks level by eye. The padlock locks again 60 seconds after your last press, and when you leave the page, a job starts, or the tool is swapped or changed. The rear centre screw moved up 0.1 mm, with the panel unlocked These moves have no limits and no endstops. Watch the bed while you press, and if a screw binds or the bed racks, press Stop . The first move marks Z as not homed and drops the saved park height, so nothing else moves Z until you home again.

sections.title: Turning a screw by hand
sections.text: Release to turn by hand switches the ticked motors off, after asking, so you can turn their lead screws by hand. The bed may settle at those screws. Hold , or the next move, switches them back on. Releasing asks first and shows the command A screw whose motor is off is drawn with a dashed ring, and its card says motor off . Klipper also switches every motor off after the machine has been idle for a while, so motor off on all three screws is normal after a pause. The rear centre motor switched off: a dashed ring and 'motor off'

sections.title: Home and level
sections.text: Home all homes every axis. Level the gantry runs Z_TILT_ADJUST . It needs a print head mounted and confirmed, because it probes with the head, and X, Y and Z homed. Both ask first. The table shows each pass of the last Z-tilt: the correction each screw got and the range left across the probe points. Z-tilt repeats until the range is within its tolerance. If it stops with an error, the panel shows the error instead. Before any Z-tilt since the Rhino restarted, the panel reads NO Z_TILT PERFORMED SINCE RESTART . Two passes of Z-tilt: 0.412 mm range, then 0.021 mm When Z-tilt stops with "Move out of range" On Configuration , look at the last Z-tilt's numbers on the cards: the screw with the largest correction is the one furthest off. Tick that screw, unlock and move it until the bed looks level by eye, or release it and turn it by hand, then press Hold . Press Home all , then Level the gantry . Repeat from step 1 if it stops again. Once Z-tilt finishes, make a new bed mesh if the old one was taken before the bed was moved.

Assets holds what the Rhino is made of and works with, in three groups in the side menu. Toolheads : the Library, the Tool connector and Kinds of tool. Hardware : System hardware, Board pins and outputs, and Job hooks. Parts : Materials, Nozzles and Categories. These are the same records the Portal keeps (see The Tool Manager portal ), and every change is checked by the Portal against your whole Klipper config before it is written.

sections.title: Toolheads
sections.text: The Library shows each toolhead as a card: its picture, slot, what it does, its materials, and whether it is mounted or has maintenance due. Add a toolhead starts the wizard for a tool you have built; its steps are the same as the Portal's (see Adding a tool ). Assets › Toolheads › Library Select a card for the tool's own page: About : what the tool does, its kind, slot and outputs. Built-in tools are read-only; your own tools have Edit . Tool connector : the umbilical's contacts this tool uses, drawn on the connector. Tuning (print heads): each test's last run, per material and nozzle, and Tune (see Tuning a print head ). Start and end G-code : pick one of your macros ( Settings › Your macros ) to run after START_JOB has homed and heated, or before END_PRINT cools and parks. It is copied into the tool's job hooks; restart Klipper to make it live. If you edit the macro later, the page says so and offers Update . Macros for this tool and Use and care : its macros, its hours and jobs, and its maintenance tasks. A toolhead's page: BlockOne Tool connector shows all 21 contacts of the umbilical and what each one does for every tool; pick a tool to see only its contacts. Kinds of tool lists the kinds the Add a toolhead wizard offers, under Additive, Subtractive and Passive, with the starting values each kind fills in for a new tool. The tool connector: every contact and the tools that use it

sections.title: System hardware and the Add hardware wizard
sections.text: System hardware is anything wired to the board rather than the tool connector: enclosure fans and lights, an air or vacuum pump, a door switch. It is there whichever tool is mounted, and each item can have its own maintenance tasks. Items with live controls appear on Control › Hardware . Press Add system hardware for the wizard. It asks six short steps, with the wizard's rhino beside each question: What is it : the kind of hardware, from relays and dimmers to spindles, coolant, fans, heaters, sensors and switches. Wiring : the pins, the switch type and electrical details. Only pins that can do the job are offered. For which tools : the whole machine, a category of tools, or particular tools. Follows : what turns it on and off, such as a heater, the motors or the job. Shows : where it appears: Control, the Dashboard, macros. Check : the result is checked against your whole Klipper config, and written. It goes live after the next Klipper restart; the banner offers to restart, or waits for a job to end. Add hardware, step 1: what are you adding? To change an item later, open it and edit: its answers are filled in. To make it a different kind, remove it and add the new one.

sections.title: Board pins, Job hooks and Parts
sections.text: Board pins and outputs shows what the Klipper config does with the board: its outputs, which tools share them, and every pin it knows. Pin labels give a pin a name ( pin: NAME in any section); moving the label moves every section that uses it. Job hooks are short lists of commands Klipper runs at set points of every job, for the whole machine or one tool: before and when the job starts, before and after it ends, when it is cancelled, paused or resumed. Every line is checked as you type; Save writes job_hooks.cfg , live after the next Klipper restart. Materials , Nozzles and Categories are the names the tool wizard and the job screens offer. Add the ones you use and press its Save button ( Save material names , for example). Board pins and outputs

Care is Rhino Studio's view of the maintenance the Portal tracks: what is due, the tasks, the Task Library, the work log and the usage meters. The ideas behind it, such as Task Books, schedules by time or by use, and status codes, are explained in Part 5, Maintenance tracking . Care informs; it never stops a job.

sections.title: Overview
