sections.text: The counts across the top: overdue, due soon, on hold, and the production hours the Portal has counted from Klipper and Moonraker. Below are the tasks that need doing, most urgent first, and a card for each toolhead with its next task. On a task, Log work records it done, with notes; Snooze 7 days puts it off; Set status gives it a status code such as Waiting on parts . Care › Overview: what is due, and each toolhead's next task

sections.title: Tasks and the Task Library
sections.text: Tasks lists every task, grouped by what it's for, with filters for status and tool. Select a task to change its schedule, steps or parts; New task adds one of your own. The Task Library holds ready-made Task Books: put one on a toolhead, a machine area or the whole machine with Assign , and its tasks are added, still linked, so editing a library task updates every copy. The Task Library: ready-made Task Books

sections.title: Work log and usage meters
sections.text: The Work log lists everything done, skipped, set or measured, newest first; each entry keeps the meter readings of its moment, so schedules restart from the right place. Usage meters shows the machine's and each tool's hours, jobs, filament and swaps; a meter can be set by hand, for a part changed outside the log. The switch at the bottom shows overdue and due-soon tasks after Klipper starts, once, after the which-tool question. PM_STATUS in the console lists them any time. The work log Care setup holds the lists tasks choose from: Status codes , and Areas, kinds and priorities .
Settings has three groups. The pages under Machine and System change the Rhino for every screen; Appearance is shared too, except the day-or-night choice, which is for the screen you're on.

sections.title: Appearance
sections.text: Look follows this device, or holds it to Dark or Light. Theme picks the colours every screen shares. Your own themes can have a background picture ( Add picture… , up to 12 kept on the Rhino; dimmed so panels stay readable), a text colour, and typefaces for titles, subheadings and regular text; each is kept with the theme, for day and night. The 3D view slider sets how see-through the bed is from below, for seeing support marks. Settings › Appearance Whatever the theme, Stop and a live panel stay red, and the big numbers, positions and console keep their own fonts. A shared theme file names its picture but doesn't carry it, so on another Rhino it shows the plain page colour.

sections.title: Machine
sections.text: Connection : where this screen finds Moonraker and the Portal. Leave the boxes blank when Studio is opened from the Rhino. Trusted addresses : which screens Moonraker lets in, the same list Mainsail uses. Tool changing : how this machine changes tools and how Studio reads which one is mounted (on the Rhino, SWAP_TOOL ). Cameras : the camera list Moonraker keeps for every screen; add, edit, turn off or delete a camera. Slice profiles : your slicing settings, saved on the Rhino, so a cleared browser or a new host keeps them. Rename, export, import, or go back to an earlier version with History . Your macros : short routines built from steps, saved on the Rhino and run from Control › Macros . New macro , or Add the starter macros (park, heat for PLA, cool down). What it sends now shows the G-code for the machine as it is, or why it can't run. A macro is refused during a job, with the wrong or unconfirmed tool, with an axis not homed, or past the travel limits.

sections.title: System
sections.text: Software : every package on the host, its version and the latest, with Update for each and Update all . Updates are refused while a job runs; Update all runs them in order and restarts each service once. The Rhino Tool Manager, with the Rhino Studio inside it, updates from here too. Network : how this screen reaches the Rhino, and the Rhino's own network: Wi-Fi or Ethernet, fixed or automatic address. A network change switches back by itself when its time runs out, unless you keep it, so a mistake can't lock you out. Host : restart Klipper, its firmware or a service; reboot or shut down the host; the Rhino's name on the network; and Backups (see Files, backups and tests ). Nothing here runs during a job. Host health : how hard the host and the boards are working (see below). Logs : Klipper's and Moonraker's logs, with the last error picked out. About : the Studio version, its credits, and the style guide. Settings › Software Settings › Host: restarts, the host's name and backups

sections.title: Host health
sections.text: Settings › Host health is for troubleshooting the computer beside the machine. It only reads; nothing on it changes anything. At the top, What to look at lists anything out of the ordinary in plain words: a hot or busy core, a board that is heavily loaded or resending over USB, low disk space or memory, a stopped service. When nothing is flagged it says Normal . Processor : each core's load now, with a graph of the last ten minutes and its average and peak, its temperature and clock; the package temperature, the load average, and how much of the last 10 seconds programs waited for a free core. Klipper and the boards : how much of a core Klipper uses and which cores it may run on, then each board's load, how long it is awake, bytes resent since the page opened, and the round trip over USB. A busy board, or resent bytes, is where Timer too close and lost communication start. Memory and storage : memory, swap and free disk space, and how long programs waited for memory or the disk. Programs : the Rhino's own programs (Klipper, Moonraker, the Portal, the cameras, nginx and PrusaSlicer while it slices), then the busiest others, each with its CPU share, memory, the core it last ran on and the cores it may use. Services and Other temperatures : whether each service Moonraker knows is running, and every other sensor, such as the drive and Wi-Fi card. Settings › Host health, with a hot, busy core and a stopped camera service flagged Copy report puts every reading on the page into one block of text, and Download saves it as a file. Send it with a problem report, or keep one from a good day to compare against.

The portal keeps track of preventive maintenance for the machine, every tool and the system hardware. It tells you what is overdue, what is coming up and what parts to have ready. It never blocks a job, a swap or a command. Open it from Maintenance in the sidebar: Due & upcoming , Tasks , Task Library , Work log and Usage meters .

sections.title: Getting started
sections.text: Open the Task Library and assign a Task Book to the whole machine and to each tool: Rhino motion system and frame on the machine, 3D print head on BlockOne and SwitchFly, Laser module on LightSaber, and so on. The intervals are starting points; tune them to how your machine wears (see Task Library and Task Books ). When you add a tool, the confirmation offers the book that fits it.

sections.title: Due & upcoming
sections.text: Tasks are grouped by status. The tiles at the top count them. Each card shows every rule with a progress bar, how far off it is, and an estimate in days at your usual rate of use. Once the early alarm goes off, the card lists the parts to Have ready . Due & upcoming Group Meaning Overdue Past the due point Due soon Inside the early alarm: time to plan the work and order parts A status code's own group Tasks set to a status shown in its own group, such as Pending – Waiting on parts Snoozed Put off on purpose Coming up The next eight tasks by how close they are to due, plus tasks set to a status shown with the upcoming ones Log work records what happened. Set status puts a status code on the task. Snooze puts an overdue or due-soon task off for 1 day to 2 weeks. Details opens the task. The sidebar badge and a chip in the top bar show the count: red for overdue, amber for due soon. A card with a status code set shows it at the top in its colour, with the note, when it was set and when it ends by itself. Here In progress ends after three days; the task is still due soon underneath. A task set to In progress, with its note

sections.title: Logging work
sections.text: Log work shows the task's steps and safety notes. What happened? is a list: Done ; Skipped – not needed this time if you checked and nothing needed doing; or one of your status codes. Done and Skipped start the schedule again from here, and so do a part's hours, so a new nozzle starts at zero. You can backdate the entry and add notes; the current meter readings are saved with it. Logging a nozzle clean as done Choosing a status code instead sets that status on the task and logs it. The help line says what the status does; Pending – Waiting on parts needs a note saying what is on order. Logging a task as waiting on parts Set status on a card does the same without the steps, and Clear the status takes it off again. Setting a status from the card

sections.title: Tasks
sections.text: Every task in one table, sorted overdue first, with its status code and status. Library tasks show Library and the Task Book they came from. Show filters it: overdue and due soon, with a status set, one machine area, one tool or piece of system hardware, or archived. Choosing an area or a tool also shows its usage meters. Tasks

sections.title: Creating a task
sections.text: + New task opens the task editor: Task – a short title. It is also shown in the Mainsail reminder. For – a machine area, a tool or a piece of system hardware. Kind of work and Priority – used for sorting and the card's label (the lists are under Admin › Maintenance lists ). When is it due? – up to four rules. The task is due when the first of them is reached. Start counting from (new tasks only) – now, or the date it was last done, with the meter readings at that time. How to do it – steps, parts and consumables, tools needed, time needed, safety notes and links. Reminders – include it in the start-up reminder, or pause the task. A new task with two rules Rule Example Early alarm Every so often every 3 months 14 days before After so much use every 100 working hours of this tool 10 h before After each event after each emergency stop or Klipper shutdown due straight away Once, on a date 1 Dec 2026 7 days before Time rules count from when the task was last done, so doing it late moves the next one later. Choose On a fixed calendar to keep the same dates every time, such as the 1st of every month. A usage rule's early alarm is in the meter's own unit; leave it empty for 10% of the interval. Events are a tool swap, this tool being mounted, a job, and an emergency stop or shutdown. Add this task to the Task Library , at the bottom of an existing task, turns it into a library task and links it.

sections.title: Work log
sections.text: Every entry, newest first: work done or skipped, status codes set and cleared, and meter changes. Filter it by machine area, tool or system hardware. Work log

sections.title: Usage meters
sections.text: Usage rules count these meters. The portal reads them from Moonraker every few seconds and from Moonraker's job history. Usage meters Meter Machine Each tool Counts Machine up hours yes – Klipper running and ready Production hours yes yes A job running. Pauses are not counted. Hours mounted – yes The tool on the machine while Klipper is up Working hours – yes Print heads: nozzle heater on. LightSaber: laser on. HotJoe: spindle running. Added powered tools: output on. Passive tools and DragKnife: running a job. Jobs yes yes Finished jobs, from the job history Filament used yes print heads From the job history Tool swaps / Times mounted yes yes A different tool mounted. A restart is not a swap. Emergency stops and shutdowns yes – Klipper entering shutdown The first time the portal runs, it imports the jobs already in Moonraker's history as the machine's starting reading. If the machine had hours before that, press Set on a meter and note why; the change goes in the work log. Jobs that ran while the portal was stopped are filled in from the history the next time it starts. System hardware tasks count the machine's meters. The page also has the start-up reminder switch.

sections.title: The Mainsail reminder
sections.text: After Klipper starts, once you answer which toolhead is mounted? , Klipper asks a Maintenance due question, shown on Control in Studio (and in Mainsail), with up to eight overdue and due-soon tasks, overdue first. It appears once per start; close it with OK . Snoozed tasks, tasks with the reminder unticked and tasks set to a status code that leaves them out of the reminder are not shown. The portal keeps myrhino/maintenance_status.cfg up to date, and Klipper reads it when it starts. At any other time, type PM_STATUS in the console for the live list, or PM_REMINDER to show the start-up pop-up again. Renaming a tool moves its tasks and meters with it. Removing a tool or a piece of system hardware archives its tasks (filter Archived ) and keeps their work-log entries.

The Task Library holds task definitions that are not tied to anything yet – the starter tasks for the Rhino and each kind of tool, and any you add. A Task Book is a named group of library tasks. Assign a book to a toolhead, a piece of system hardware or the whole machine, and it carries all of its tasks there. The Task Books tab shows each book, its tasks and where it is assigned. Assign... puts it on something more; the × on an assignment takes it off, which archives the tasks it added there (their work log is kept). Books whose tasks count a tool's own use, such as working hours, can only go on toolheads. Task Books, with where each is assigned Assign... asks where. Whole machine puts each task in its own machine area (belts in Motion X/Y, leadscrews in Motion Z...). Assigning a book twice adds nothing twice. Assigning a Task Book

sections.title: Linked tasks
sections.text: Tasks that come from the library stay linked to it. Their steps and schedule are the library's, so Details on a linked task shows them read-only with two choices: Edit the library task , which changes every copy at once, or Detach to customise , which turns this one task into an ordinary task you can edit on its own. Pausing a linked task affects only that task. Each copy keeps its own schedule: when it was last done, its readings and its status. A linked task The Library tasks tab lists every library task: its schedule, what it can go on, the books it is in and the tasks made from it. Edit opens the editor; saving says how many linked tasks it updates. Add to... puts one library task on something without a book. + Library task adds your own; its Area when the book goes on the whole machine decides where it lands with Whole machine . Deleting a library task keeps the tasks made from it as ordinary tasks. Library tasks Editing a library task: the box at the top lists the tasks it will update. Editing the laser-lens library task + Task Book makes a book: a name, an optional description and the library tasks in it, found with the search box. Tasks you add to a book that is already assigned are added there too; tasks you take out are archived there. A new Task Book for wide-nozzle print heads

Admin › Status codes lists two kinds of status. The built-in statuses – Overdue, Due soon, Scheduled, Done, Snoozed and Paused – are worked out from each task's schedule, the snooze and the pause switch. Rename them or change their colour; they cannot be removed. Built-in statuses: name and colour Your status codes are set by hand, from a task card or the Log work list: Pending – Waiting on parts , In progress , Deferred to next shutdown , or any you add with + Add a status code . Each answers four questions, and the portal applies the answers as rules. The rules of Pending – Waiting on parts Question Choices What it does 1. Where does the task show? With the due tasks · in its own group · with the upcoming tasks Where Due & upcoming lists it. Only with the due tasks keeps it in the overdue and due-soon counts. 2. What happens to its schedule? Keeps running · pauses · counts as done Keeps running : the task still ages toward overdue. Pauses : time and use while the status is set do not count; the due point moves later by that much when it ends. Counts as done : the interval starts again when the status is set. 3. When does it end by itself? Never · after a number of days · when the machine or tool is used again When it ends, the task goes back to its built-in status and the end is logged. Logging the task done also ends it. 4. Also Keep it in the Mainsail reminder · a note is required · offer it in the Log work list Whether the start-up pop-up still shows the task when due; whether whoever sets it must say why; whether it appears next to Done and Skipped. A status code that tasks are set to cannot be removed until they are cleared. The three codes the portal starts with: Status code Shows Schedule Ends Pending – Waiting on parts own group keeps running never (note required) In progress with the due tasks keeps running after 3 days Deferred to next shutdown with the upcoming tasks pauses when the machine is used again

Four items are scheduled in the build notes; no intervals are set yet, so record what you find and when. Item What to do XY belts Check for stretch and uneven tension; re-tension as below. Replacements: 15 mm GT2, glass-fibre core, 3 m per belt Bearings and rails Check the X rail and the bearings in the idlers and tensioners for roughness or play Z leadscrews Clean and re-lubricate all three leadscrews Under the bed Clear dust, chips and filament from the underside of the machine

sections.title: Tensioning the XY belts
sections.text: Each belt has a cam tensioner on the rear frame bar with an adjustment knob that indexes into one of five settings. Belt tensioner assembly, exploded (item 14 is the adjustment knob) Loosen both belt clamps on the X-carriage. Turn both tensioners to their lowest setting. Pull each belt through its carriage clamp until it is snug with no slack – not tight – while keeping the gantry square to both Y rails. The holes in the linear rails are a quick reference. Tighten the belt clamps. Turn both tensioner knobs to the same setting.

sections.title: Tramming the bed
sections.text: With a print head mounted, home with G28 , then run Z_TILT_ADJUST . Klipper probes three points and levels the bed with its three Z motors, retrying up to five times until the points agree within 0.05 mm. Run it after any work on the leadscrews or the bed.

sections.title: Calibrating the spindle ESC
sections.text: Do this once when an ESC is new or replaced, or if spindle speeds look wrong. Remove the bit from the collet first. Mount HotJoe and run CALIBRATE_ESC . Press Step 2: Send full throttle (signal 1.0). This switches the spindle relay on with a full-throttle signal, so the ESC powers up and plays its start-up tones. As soon as the tones finish, press Step 4: Send low endpoint (signal 0.3). The ESC confirms with a tone. Its throttle range now matches Klipper's 0.3–1.0.

Symptom Likely cause Fix Mainsail's Resume says extruder not hot enough A non-print tool's job is paused Use Resume job in the Rhino pop-up, or TOOL_RESUME Console: resume it with TOOL_RESUME after pressing Resume Same – the extruder happened to be warm TOOL_RESUME Job refuses to start: HARDWARE MISMATCH File sliced for a different tool than the one recorded START_TOOL_SWAP to the right tool, or answer the restart pop-up correctly Laser or spindle command: CRITICAL SAFETY BLOCK Recorded tool is not LightSaber / HotJoe Check the restart pop-up answer; run RESTORE_TOOL New tool not listed in Studio / Unknown command Klipper not restarted since adding it Restart Klipper from Studio's banner, or RESTART_FOR_TOOLS Portal shows Moonraker offline Moonraker stopped, or portal pointed at the wrong address Restart Moonraker; the portal still edits tools but cannot restart Klipper Portal: Restarting now would kill it A job is printing or paused Wait for the job to finish or cancel it REMOVE_TOOLHEAD : is the mounted tool You cannot remove the tool on the machine Swap to another tool first Tool commands: blocked while a job is printing Registry changes are locked during jobs Finish or cancel the job Add wizard offers no free pins All three free connector pins (PB1, PC0, PC1) are taken Share an existing output, or list more umbilical pins in myrhino/umbilical.json Swap wizard: Toolhead not detected Umbilical not seated Re-seat the 21-pin umbilical and press Check again Added tool switched itself off Watchdog: on longer than Max time on with no job Raise Max time on in the portal, or run it from a job file ABS/ASA bed cooldown stops early Klipper's 600 s idle timeout Add [idle_timeout] with timeout: 1800 rhino_toolgen or backup commands fail Login is not pi Fix the /home/pi paths (see Install ) Swap wizard stays on Cooling down It waits until the hotend and the bed are both below 40 °C Wait; after a hot print the bed is usually the slow one Drag-knife file stops with M3 rejected The CAM profile writes laser power commands Use a drag-knife LaserWeb profile with Laser Intensity and Tool Off blank Spindle speed range wrong, or ESC will not arm ESC endpoints not calibrated to Klipper's 0.3–1.0 signal Run CALIBRATE_ESC with the bit removed Control or macro refused: already exists The name is used by another macro, a Klipper command or a config object (Klipper ignores case for macros) Choose another name; the message says who has it A pin is greyed out in the controls guide umbilical.json marks it as a MOSFET output, which cannot read a signal or drive a servo Use a logic pin, or correct the pin's type Banner says time left unknown The file has no slicer estimate and is under 2% done Wait a moment; it estimates from progress after that Meters do not move The portal service is not running (meters are counted by it) sudo systemctl status rhino-portal ; missed jobs are filled in from the history when it starts No maintenance pop-up after a restart Nothing was due, the reminder is switched off, or the tool-restore question was not answered yet Answer the question, or run PM_STATUS

To change one thing, open the one file that owns it. To change Edit Built-in tools, their materials and slots variables.cfg Positions: park, tool swap, safe height, Set Z zero limit, prime line myrhino/positions.cfg - the one place; every macro reads it Your added tools The portal or console commands (stored in myrhino/custom_tools.json ; custom_tools.cfg is generated – never edit it) Starting values, caps, checklists, allowed characters rhino/presets.py Which pins reach the tool connector myrhino/umbilical.json (copy umbilical.example.json ) M3 / M5 , power cap, watchdog, safe-off, pause/resume tools/tool_power.cfg What Pause / Resume / Cancel add to Mainsail's buttons _CLIENT_VARIABLE and _RHINO_CANCEL in client_macros.cfg Tool swap and restart prompt toolchanger.cfg , guided/tool_swap_wizard.cfg Job setup wizards guided/*_workflow.cfg Portal screens rhino/portal/static/portal.js , templates/index.html , portal.css A tool's controls and macros The portal (Controls and Macros tabs). They are written into custom_tools.cfg ; the rules are in rhino/extras.py Maintenance tasks, work log, meters The portal. Stored in myrhino/maintenance/ (tasks.json, history.json, meters.json), so the GitHub backup keeps them Starter task intervals rhino/maint/library.py (only affects tasks added afterwards) The start-up maintenance pop-up guided/maintenance.cfg ; myrhino/maintenance_status.cfg is generated - never edit it Positions. Where the head parks, where it goes for a tool swap, how far the bed lowers before a swap or park, the lowest the Set Z zero window goes, and where the prime line starts and how long it is are all in myrhino/positions.cfg . Change a number, save, then FIRMWARE_RESTART ; every macro (and Mainsail's own pause park) uses the new number. Type RHINO_POSITIONS in the console to list them - it also checks each one against the travel limits in printer.cfg , and the same check runs at every start with any problem shown in red. Updates never overwrite this file. The travel limits themselves, where Z homes and the probe offset stay in printer.cfg because Klipper needs them; the paper test goes to the probe's spot worked out from those. Backups. BACKUP_CFG MSG=<note> pushes the config folder to your GitHub backup through klipper-backup. The tool registry keeps its last 10 versions in myrhino/registry_backups/ . Photos live outside the config folder in ~/printer_data/rhino_data/images/ , so they are not in the GitHub backup. Tests. sh dev/run_all.sh runs a static check of the whole config and 619 automated checks: the macros in a simulated Klipper (against the real Mainsail macros); motion tests that follow where the bed and head go and run every macro and button from seven machine states with each toolhead against five safety rules; the portal, tool controls and macros, maintenance and the Admin lists; every portal screen opened in a real browser, with an accessibility scan and keyboard checks; and the installer run on a fake Pi. It needs pip install jinja2 flask (and Playwright for the browser test), and runs on every change pushed to GitHub. The simulator knows the travel limits, not the shape of your tools or stock, so every release also has on-machine checks - the plan is in docs/testing.md , and the ones for the current version are in Still to check on the machine . Trying the portal without the printer. python3 dev/demo_server.py runs the portal against a copy of the config and a pretend Moonraker. Every screen in this manual can be tried there without touching the machine.

still-to-check-on-the-machine.title: Still to check on the machine

sections.text: The automated tests can't move the machine, so each release is checked on it. Work through these in order, with a hand on the emergency stop; stop at any test that doesn't pass and note its number. The full plan, with what counts as a pass and when to stop, is in docs/testing.md in both repos. This list is what hasn't been signed off on the OptiPlex 7050 as of Tool Manager 1.9.18.

sections.title: Install and start
sections.text: A1 Install the next release from Settings › Software – every step ticks, Studio reloads on the new version, and the Portal answers. A2 FIRMWARE_RESTART with a print head mounted – Klipper ready, no config errors. A3 The which toolhead is mounted? question appears; CHECK_TOOLHEADS lists every tool. A5 Studio opens at http://rhinostudio.local on a PC and a phone, and Settings › Software shows the new version.

sections.title: Motion and homing
sections.text: B1 Jog X and Y 100 mm and measure – 100 mm ±0.5. About 50 mm means a step setting is wrong: stop and report it. B2 Jog Z 10 mm and measure – 10 mm ±0.1 (gear_ratio 2:1). Then Z_TILT_ADJUST . B5 Cancel a print – the bed lowers to Z150 or more, X/Y home, the head parks at X551 Y381 without touching the frame. B5b Cancel a laser job (new in 1.4.5) – laser and rail off, bed lowers, no X/Y homing, the head goes straight to X551 Y381. If X or Y starts homing, report it. B6 Z travel (new in 1.4.3): home with BlockOne, G1 Z290 F600 – the bed stays clear of its mounts – then G1 Z300 is refused and nothing moves. If the bed touches a mount at Z290, stop and send the Z where it is 10 mm clear.

sections.title: Homing guard and positions (new in 1.3.8 and 1.4.0)
sections.text: A6 LightSaber mounted: Home all on Control is refused with a message and nothing moves. Home X and Home Y work once the Y endstop is set for the LightSaber. BlockOne mounted: Home All homes as before. C4 Restart with the bed parked, then swap: the console says homing X/Y lowered the bed 10 mm and the park height was updated; SET_Z_ZERO then shows the new height. A7 RHINO_POSITIONS lists the positions and says they are inside the travel limits. Change park_x in myrhino/positions.cfg to 540, restart, cancel a print: the head parks at X540. Put it back.

sections.title: Tool swaps
sections.text: C1 Swap BlockOne to LightSaber – waits for 40 °C, lowers the bed, never homes Z. C2 During a swap, unplug the umbilical – Klipper keeps running (the nozzle reads about −50 °C). Confirm while it is unplugged: Toolhead not detected ; plug in, Check again . C5 With LightSaber mounted, 200 in the nozzle temperature box is refused. C3 Start a BlockOne file with the laser mounted – refused, nothing moves.

sections.title: Printing
sections.text: D1–D3 Paper test, then a test cube with the Orca profiles: the PLA question closes when answered, 210/65 °C, a 120 mm prime line, a slow first layer, the bed parked and the head at X551 Y381 at the end (1.4.4). The first layer is laid at the paper-test height (fixed in 1.3.8).

sections.title: SwitchFly materials and the end of a job (new in 1.4.6)
sections.text: D4 Start a SwitchFly file – it waits on Path 2 (T1) material? with path 1 from the file shown; nothing moves after homing. D5 The confirmation lists both paths and the path it prints from; Proceed heats, primes and prints. D6 Start it again – Same as last time is the first button, also after FIRMWARE_RESTART . D7 Cancel at the path question – the job shows cancelled, nothing heats. D8 SWITCH_T1 by hand loads and purges with path 2's material (no PLA default); SWITCH_T0 MATERIAL=NYLON is refused and nothing moves. D9 An item ticked switch off when made safe stays on after a normal finish (print and laser), and goes off on cancel.

sections.title: The record follows the tool (new in 1.4.7)
sections.text: D10 Swap SwitchFly back on after leaving it on path 2 – the selector turns to path 1 and G1 E5 feeds in. D11 Restart, answer Yes – SwitchFly – nothing moves, path 2 still feeds in. D12 Swap to BlockOne after SwitchFly path 2 – G1 E5 feeds in.

sections.title: Set Z zero
sections.text: E1–E2 SET_Z_ZERO with LightSaber or HotJoe – the buttons move the bed the amount shown, Bed down stops at Z290, SET moves nothing, and G1 Z5 F300 then lifts the tool 5 mm above the surface. E3 Restart with the bed parked, run SET_Z_ZERO – the Bed position question; Yes – the bed doesn't move, X/Y home, then the Set Z zero window opens. Needs [force_move] enable_force_move: True (in toolchanger.cfg ). E4 Restart after moving the bed below Z150 – no question; home Z with a print head. E6 After a CNC or drag-knife setup, swap to BlockOne and print – no X/Y shift.

sections.title: Laser, CNC and drag-knife jobs
sections.text: F1–F3 Laser at low power on scrap; a CNC air cut 10 mm above the stock first; a drag-knife test line. Run the first file from the LaserWeb settings in Slicer and CAM settings at low power. F4 Pause and resume each tool type – the 10 mm lift clears the work, and the spindle is back to speed before it re-enters the cut. Power values – tune every placeholder power and on-time on the real tools.

sections.title: Emergency stop and backups
sections.text: H1–H2 EMERGENCY_STOP with the focus dot on – laser off at once; with HotJoe – relay open, ESC quiet. I1 Klipper-Backup shows your config files in GitHub again after removing the stray .git folder.

sections.title: Settings to know
sections.text: Idle timeout – add [idle_timeout] timeout: 1800 if you use the full ABS/ASA cooldown. Connector pins – only PB1, PC0 and PC1 are free; list any other spare umbilical pins in myrhino/umbilical.json . LEDFLASH takes about 1.35 s, which also delays the macros that call it (cancel, emergency stop).

sections.title: Network settings (new in 1.4.8)
sections.text: N1–N4 Read the network; power saving off with Keep, Undo now, and letting the 2-minute timer switch it back. N5–N7 Rename, fixed address kept from the new address, and a wrong address that switches back by itself. N8 Changes refused during a print.

sections.title: PrusaSlicer on the Rhino
sections.text: P3–P6 Slice a part, check the Rhino's start and temperatures are in the file, a newer slice stops the older one (and its sandbox), and the same slice again comes from the cache. P7 Slicing during a print: half the cores on a bigger host, refused on a Pi 3B; the print keeps going smoothly. P8–P9 Updating the engine from Flathub, and going back to the version before.

sections.title: Rhino Studio from the Rhino
sections.text: S4–S6 A change through the Portal is accepted, the camera shows, and a job reaches Files. S7 Undo takes Studio's site away again and leaves Mainsail working.

sections.title: Your macros and start and end G-code (1.9.13)
sections.text: MB1–MB3 Add the starter macros; Heat for PLA runs without asking; Park the head asks first and goes to the park spot. MB4–MB5 Park refused with the tool not confirmed; a move past the travel refused before sending; editing on a phone. MB6–MB8 Park as a tool's start G-code runs after START_JOB; Update after editing the macro; restoring only Your macros from a backup.

sections.title: Print head tuning (1.9.16 and 1.9.17)
sections.text: TU1 Extruder calibration on BlockOne: asks first, pushes 100 mm, and saves the new rotation distance. The push itself takes about 100 s (seen Nov 9). TU2–TU3 The next print says rotation distance … (tuned) at job start; the result shows on the tool's page and comes back from a backup. TU4–TU6 First-layer squish, pressure advance and extrusion multiplier tests print where the manual says, and the chosen value is saved. TU7 With no gcodes/tuning/ folder yet, Make the test creates it and says Sent as tuning/… . TA1–TA5 At job start the console says which values are tuned and which come from printer.cfg ; stored values reach variables.cfg ; an untuned material goes back to the defaults; a desktop-slicer file gets the tuned pressure advance.

sections.title: Bed › Configuration (Studio, Nov 8)
sections.text: BC1 The bed drawing shows the three screws and the Z-tilt probe points where they really are. BC2–BC3 Up and Down move only the ticked screws, by the step. Up raises the bed (seen Nov 9); still to see each motor on its own and two together. BC4–BC5 Release lets a screw turn by hand without the bed sinking; the panel locks after 60 s, on leaving the page and on a tool swap. BC6 The next time Z-tilt faults out, level the bed by eye with the screws, then Home all and Level the gantry succeed.

sections.title: Wiring to confirm
sections.text: Spindle and servo PWM contact. The umbilical pin map puts the ESC signal (PB11) on contact 18, but the original HotJoe and SwitchFly sheets listed the PWM signal on contact 19. This manual and the portal use 18, which matches the pin map and printer.cfg ; check the connector and correct the pages if it is 19. Laser 12 V power pin. The pin map lists PD12 (Fan2) for the 12 V power activate on contacts 20–21; printer.cfg drives LASER_INITIALIZE from PD13 (Fan3 on the Octopus v1.1). X and Y endstops. The wiring sheets give X-limit PG6 and Y-limit PG9; printer.cfg has stepper_x on PG9 and stepper_y on PG6. SwitchFly servo power. The SwitchFly page lists 24 V power activate on contacts 11–12, while its servo wiring diagram feeds the regulator from 12 V activate. Fan labels. On the Octopus v1.1 PA8 is FAN0 and PE5 is FAN1; the pin sheets label them Fan5 and Fan0. The pins are right; only the labels differ.
